summary: Round 44 READ-TIME DRY RUN (17:14-17:30Z, 0 Kaggle calls). exp89t 56669888 was PENDING at the 17:15:03Z header. mk_card_1837.py is intact (a19e1bd6, --dry-all 35/35). A single read-time block, scratchpad r44dry/readtime.sh, now covers every outcome. It takes the R43-A4 awk first terminal header, computes L_lo/L_hi with the +210 s x F rule, sets the code under decision B, reads SELECTED per R43-A3 wrapped in timeout 90, applies the R39-A4 comparator, builds the card with the R41-A4 inputs, and applies the R43-A5 rank line and the R43-A4 ins-tail note. It then prints the pre-registered Russian push text for case a or b. It was dry-run on 11 fake poll.log outcomes (T1, T1 with an error-tagged data block, T1 with ins-tail, T2, T3KEEP, T3KEEP late, T5, T5 late, T6, T8, [manual-admit] -> T2, PENDING/T7/admit-pending) and on 6 SELECTED variants (П3, П2, a failed read twice, 1 ref, {#37,#38}); all passed the builder guard and the token checks. The real builder was not touched and no real card file was written. Defects found: (1) the Bash tool keeps no state between calls, and sourcing under a pipe loses the functions, so each event must be one call; (2) an undefined 'msg' helper falls through to Windows MSG.exe, so the helper is renamed pushtext44; (3) read_selected.py has no timeout, so it must always run under 'timeout 90', and a timeout counts as a failed read; (4) the rank-line count is 4 003 (Overview) or 4 005 (LB rows), which is cosmetic; (5) the header-keyed and L_hi-keyed edges differ only in two 3.5-min windows that no projected header hits; (6) --lb post_exp89t no longer matters. Concurs with R44-PC-02 (do not start round 45 before the read and the card). No new idea reaches R8.

findings.what: Two traps found in the dry run. (a) The Bash tool does not keep shell state between calls. Also, '. readtime.sh | grep …' runs the source in a subshell, so HL/CODE/SEL and the functions are lost. The block must be sourced without a pipe, in the same call that runs cardcmd, cardfix and pushtext44. (b) An undefined helper named 'msg' falls through to Windows MSG.exe, which in the test printed its cp866 help text. Given arguments, it could send a broadcast message. The helper is therefore named pushtext44. The main session must not write any ad-hoc function called msg.
findings.evidence: Dry-run transcript 17:22Z: 'environment: line 10: cardcmd: command not found' followed by the MSG.exe usage text when the source ran under a pipe; after renaming and dropping the pipe, all scenarios ran.
findings.action: Use the command blocks as written: one call, source line on its own. For a retry after a failed SELECTED read in a later call, source the block again, which costs one more read.
